This is an essay written by an international student.

I came to Japan two years ago. I thought Japan was a very easy and convenient country to live in because it has so many convenience stores and supermarkets.

However, there is one unfortunate thing: there is a great deal of trash. When walking through the city, there is almost no litter and everything is clean, but once you live in Japan, a great deal of trash is produced. For example, when buying sweets, each individual sweet is wrapped in a plastic bag inside the package. Every time you eat one, the amount of trash increases by one piece. The other day, when I bought tomatoes at a supermarket, they were placed on a plastic tray and wrapped in a plastic bag. When I got home and cooked them, both the plastic tray and the plastic bag became trash. As a result, the trash can in my home quickly became full of plastic waste.

It is true that sweets and tomatoes look clean and attractive this way, and it is convenient for people who live alone. However, I do not think it is necessary to put each sweet or tomato in a plastic bag or on a plastic tray. If plastic bags and plastic products were not used, （　　）.

default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t12-q1.explanation: The pattern ～てくれたら means “if you do something for me” and expresses a condition; 教えてくれたら means “if Kim tells me”. The pattern ～ておきます describes doing something in advance for preparation, so 予約しておきます means “will reserve it in advance”. The supporting sentence is: 「キムさんが食事に行ける日を教えてくれたら、私がレストランを予約しておきます。」, meaning “If Kim tells me which day she can go out to eat, I will reserve a restaurant in advance.” To distinguish the choices, (c) is the information Kim must provide, while (d) is the action Tanaka will take.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t13-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 生活していると、ゴミがたくさん出ること
The writer thinks it is unfortunate that a lot of garbage is produced while living in Japan. This idea appears immediately after 「残念なことがあります」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t13-q1.explanation: 「残念なこと」 means “an unfortunate or regrettable thing” and introduces a problem the speaker is dissatisfied with. The pattern 「～と、～」 in 「生活していると、ゴミがたくさん出ます」 expresses a result that occurs when or while someone is living. Translation of the supporting sentence: “When living in Japan, a lot of garbage is produced.” Original sentence: 「日本で生活していると、たくさんゴミが出ます。」 Tip for distinguishing the choices: in 「町の中」 there is 「ゴミはほとんどなくて」, whereas 「日本で生活していると」 results in 「たくさんゴミが出ます」; therefore, (d) is correct, not (b) or (c).

✅ Correct answer: (d) おかしやトマトを一つひとつビニールやプラスチックでつつむこと

The supporting sentence is: 「確かにそうすると、おかしやトマトはきれいだし、1人で生活する人に便利です。」 To distinguish it from the easily confused option (b), remember that throwing away the packaging is a later consequence, whereas (d) describes the action referred to by 「そうする」.

✅ Correct answer: (a) ゴミは減るはずです。

✅ Correct answer: (c) 作らなくなりました
Recently, Grandma no longer makes cakes very often because she became ill two years ago.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t8-q2.explanation: The pattern 「Vなくなる」 means “to come to no longer do V,” showing a change from doing something before to not doing it now; 「あまり」 is commonly used with a negative form to mean “not very much.” The sentence means: “However, recently Grandma no longer makes cakes very often because she became ill two years ago.” The original evidence is: 「しかし、最近おばあちゃんはあまりケーキを作らなくなりました。2年前に病気になったからです。」. default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t8-q3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) だから
Because the grandmother became ill, she has not been making many cakes recently; therefore, Maria learned how to make cakes from her.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t8-q3.explanation: The pattern 「だから、～」 means “therefore/so” and introduces a result based on the preceding statement. The previous sentence says that the grandmother became ill two years ago, so Maria learned how to make cakes from her. default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t8-q4.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 作れるようになりました
After practicing a lot, Maria became able to make delicious cakes like her grandmother. The pattern 「～られるようになりました」 expresses a change from being unable to do something to being able to do it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t8-q4.explanation: The pattern 「V-potential + ようになりました」 means “became able to do V” and expresses a change in ability; 「作れる」 is the potential form of 「作る」. default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t8-q5.verdict:
